variants.label: Pivoting properly
variants.verdictText: Legal. The pivot foot never lifts or slides, however far the rest of you goes.

captions.text: You catch it and plant one foot. That foot is now your pivot.
Step wide to the open side — reach right past a defender.
Swing all the way back the other way.
The free foot went everywhere. The pivot never moved.

variants.label: Switching feet
variants.verdictText: Travel. Once you've established a pivot, that foot can't change.

captions.text: Same start — pivot planted, stepping out to throw.
So far this is all perfectly legal.
Then you plant the other foot and lift the first one…
That's a travel. You only ever get one pivot foot.

variants.label: Never planting
variants.verdictText: Travel. After catching you must slow down and plant a pivot, without changing direction.

captions.text: You catch it moving and just… keep going.
Both feet are still moving. No pivot was ever established.
Travel — and the most common one at beginner level.

variants.label: Released in two
variants.verdictText: Legal. Catch, at most two more ground contacts, and the disc is gone before a third.

captions.text: Sprinting onto a pass — no need to stop at all.
The catch itself is where the count starts.
One ground contact after the catch is fine…
…and a second. That's your limit — throw now.
Released before a third contact. Perfectly legal.

variants.label: Three contacts
variants.verdictText: Travel. Two additional ground contacts is the maximum before the disc must be gone.

captions.text: Identical catch, identical speed.
One… two… so far so good.
But a third contact lands before the throw goes.
Travel. Count contacts, not strides.

variants.label: Curving to get free
variants.verdictText: Travel. While slowing down you must not change direction to gain a better angle.

captions.text: You catch it running flat out down the line.
Now you need to slow down — in a straight line.
Instead you curl inwards to open up a better throw.
Travel. Decelerate straight, then pivot.

variants.label: A good mark
variants.verdictText: Legal. Arms wide and active, but a clear disc's width off the thrower's torso.

captions.text: The marker sets up about a forearm off the thrower.
Arms wide to take away throwing lanes — that's all legal.
They shuffle with the pivot but never close the gap.

variants.label: Disc space
variants.verdictText: Disc space. No part of the marker may be within one disc diameter of your torso.

captions.text: Starting legally, a clear gap to the thrower.
They creep in, and their body crosses the ring.
Call "disc space" — play carries on, they back off.
Gap restored. Legal again, count resumes one lower.

variants.label: Straddle
variants.verdictText: Straddle. A line between the marker's feet came within a disc's width of your pivot point.

captions.text: The marker steps right in on the pivot.
Now your pivot foot sits between their two feet.
That's a straddle — an infraction, even without contact.

variants.label: Wrapping
variants.verdictText: Wrapping. The marker's arms closed around your torso — illegal even if they never touch you.

captions.text: A normal mark, arms spread wide.
Then they curl both arms in around your body.
Wrapping. Mark with your arms out, not around.

variants.label: Guarding someone
variants.verdictText: Legal. A second defender may stand this close — as long as they're genuinely guarding another player.

captions.text: A second defender drops in toward the thrower.
They're inside three metres — but marking the cutter.
Completely legal. This is how every zone defence works.

variants.label: Guarding nobody
variants.verdictText: Double team. Inside three metres of the pivot without guarding anyone — any offensive player can call it.

captions.text: Same start — the poacher drops in again.
But this time they leave their cutter and crowd the thrower.
Nobody is being guarded. That's a double team.

variants.label: Close enough to count
variants.verdictText: Legal. Within three metres of the pivot, so the stall count runs.

captions.text: "Stalling one, two, three…"
They can move around freely inside the ring.
The count keeps running the whole time.

variants.label: Too far away
variants.verdictText: No count. Beyond three metres the marker must stop counting, and restarts at one on returning.

captions.text: The count starts legally, close to the pivot.
They chase a cutter and drift outside three metres.
The count must stop — there's no clock on you now.
Back inside, and it restarts at "Stalling one".

variants.label: Land in, drift out
variants.verdictText: Good catch. You landed in-bounds first — momentum taking you out afterwards doesn't matter.

captions.text: Chasing a pass drifting towards the sideline.
You catch it in the air — feet still off the ground.
First contact lands inside the line. That's what counts.
Now momentum carries you out. Doesn't matter.
Walk back and pivot where you crossed the line.

variants.label: Landing on the line
variants.verdictText: Turnover. The perimeter line is not part of the field, so landing on it is out.

captions.text: Same catch, a metre further across.
Airborne catch again, looking good…
…but the first foot lands on the sideline itself.
Out. Unusually for a field sport, the line is not in.

variants.label: Catching while out
variants.verdictText: Turnover, and no catch is deemed to have happened at all.

captions.text: This time you run out first, then reach back in.
Both feet are already over the line…
…when you make contact with the disc.
Turnover. If any part of you is out, you can't catch it.

variants.label: Clean catch
variants.verdictText: Goal. No contact, and all ground contact was inside the end zone.

captions.text: A pass into the end zone, defender trailing.
You catch it cleanly, no contact at all.
Both feet down inside the end zone. Goal.

variants.label: Pushed out
variants.verdictText: Force-out foul. The contact made you land out instead of in — if it would have been a goal, you get the goal.

captions.text: Identical pass, identical run.
But the defender makes contact as you're catching…
…and it carries you across the line instead of down.
Force-out. Only call it if contact changed where you landed.

own-end-zone.title: Turnover in your own end zone

variants.label: Throw from here
variants.verdictText: Legal. Staying put, or faking a pass, commits you to the pivot right where the disc was.

captions.text: You pick up a turnover deep in your own end zone.
Stay where you are — or fake a pass — and you've chosen.
Your pivot is here now. Can catch an unset defence out.

variants.label: Take it to the line
variants.verdictText: Also legal. Moving straight off commits you to the nearest point on the goal line.

captions.text: Same turnover, same spot.
Raise an arm to signal, then walk straight out.
Moving off commits you to the goal line option.
Pivot here instead — more field for your team to use.

variants.label: Changing your mind
variants.verdictText: Not allowed. Whichever option you commit to first cannot be reversed.

captions.text: You start walking out — that's the goal line option.
Then you spot a deep look and turn back…
…but you already committed by moving.
You can't reverse it. Decide before you pick the disc up.

brick.title: A pull that lands out of bounds

variants.label: Take the brick
variants.verdictText: Legal. The brick mark is one end-zone length in from your goal line, in the centre.

captions.text: The pull sails out without touching anyone.
It crosses the sideline here and lands out.
Raise an arm and call "brick" before picking it up.
Then walk to the mark in the middle of the field.
Far better than starting trapped on a sideline.

variants.label: Take the sideline
variants.verdictText: Also legal. You may instead start where the disc crossed the perimeter line.

captions.text: Exactly the same pull, out of bounds again.
You can simply take it where it crossed the line.
Quicker to start — but you're stuck on a sideline.

variants.label: Caught together
variants.verdictText: Offence keeps it. A genuinely simultaneous catch always goes to the offence.

captions.text: Both players attack the same floating disc.
They get hands on it at the exact same instant.
Tie goes to the offence — every time.

variants.label: Defender got there first
variants.verdictText: Turnover. If the defender establishes possession first, it's simply an interception.

captions.text: Same disc in the air, same two players.
This time the defender clearly has it first.
That's not simultaneous — it's just an interception.
